title: John Smith
dek: A member of the first Gate company who turns protective urgency into recruitment, shared training and an attempt to make Pristinia capable of defending itself.

facts.Name: Introduces himself as John Smith; usually addressed as John
facts.Early company: First Called · Day 1 of the Final War
facts.Civic work: Recruitment and training plans with Rolen, Melian and other townspeople
facts.Open record: Later command, departure and fate remain unestablished

body:
John Smith arrives with wings, a tail and confidence in the importance of the moment. He is quick to offer protection and quicker to become impatient when the company does not move. His early history joins the urgency of a fighter to the slower task of helping strangers become a town.

Getting the first company moving

John introduces himself beside Jiangshi and offers her protection while asking for hers. He wants to know what can kill the Wyrm and where the newcomers can establish themselves. When the gods vanish, he urges the group toward the promised village before darkness.

In the first fighting he uses height and ranged attacks, tells companions to burn the undead and spends blood magic against the shadow threatening them. The attack carries a cost to him. He has entered the war as someone who expects to act, without yet understanding everything his new enemies can do.

A home he is ready to defend

John soon speaks of Pristinia as his home. When threats gather near the roads and docks, he wants to return with proof that they have been removed. He fights beside Rolen and later vouches for Talon’s contribution against the bandits.

His confidence can become possessive and severe: he frames hostility toward the settlement as hostility toward what is his. Alongside it is a willingness to discuss diplomacy and ask Melian how she wants to respond to the outsiders. He has martial habits, but the town’s decisions are not his alone.

Recruiting people who already live there

John proposes patrols and a militia drawn from willing townspeople. He speaks of his combat training, seeks Melian’s permission to recruit at the tavern, pays for the opportunity and buys a communal meal. His speech asks residents to protect the homes and families for which they have begun to work.

He reports eleven recruits and brings the problem to Rolen. Training, equipment, farming and quarry labor must share a small pool of people. John suggests an allocation and asks Rolen to train some recruits in more precise work. These are practical negotiations and proposals, not proof that every later militia office or force was already created.

An organization that changes while he is away

When John returns to a larger gathering, the numbers and possible roles have changed. He has to ask what happened to the five militia recruits he last knew about, consult Rolen and consider whether horses could make a mounted unit possible. The exchange shows a community continuing to organize without waiting for a single adventurer to remain present.

His plans need equipment and other people’s labor. He helps establish a direction for defense; the record does not make him the sole builder of Pristinia’s institutions or establish a lifetime command.

A promise he will not make cheaply

John calls for Jako at the gathering, and their reunion interrupts the organizational discussion. He says he went away to handle danger so Jako could be safe, then admits that the attempt had nearly gone badly.

When Jako wants him to remain, he refuses an assurance he cannot keep while Death is undefeated. He will do his best to come back to Jako and the town. The answer leaves affection and duty in tension rather than resolving them with a promise the history cannot guarantee. Read Jako’s history →
